source.author: ov
source.text: Utque novus serpens posita cum pelle senecta luxuriare solet squamaque nitere recenti, sic, ubi mortales Tirynthius exuit artus, parte sui meliore viget maiorque videri coepit et augusta fieri gravitate verendus.
source.text_original: Utque novus serpens posita cum pelle senecta / luxuriare solet squamaque nitere recenti, / sic, ubi mortales Tirynthius exuit artus, / parte sui meliore viget maiorque videri / coepit et augusta fieri gravitate verendus.
source.text_english: And just as a new snake, when its old skin has been shed, is wont to grow luxuriant and gleam with fresh scales, so, when Tirynthius cast off his mortal frame, he flourished in his better part and began to seem greater and to become awe-inspiring with majestic dignity.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_original: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis / advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno / tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus / gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum / par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_english: Straightway the Tirynthian flies of his own accord to Argos of Inachus, where Hylas carries for him the poisoned darts and the bows that delight his eager shoulders—Arcadian weapons: he would indeed wish it, but his right hand is not yet equal to the burden, nor able to bear the club.
